description: Renovate covers what Dependabot cannot see in this repo: the CORE_REF git-SHA pin in the Dockerfile, which no manifest describes, and the Dockerfile base and build-stage images.

Python is deliberately left to Dependabot. requirements.txt is a hash-locked pip-compile output installed with --require-hashes, and it carries no pip-compile header, so Renovate cannot regenerate the hashes and would leave the lock inconsistent.
renault-api is Dependabot's too, in its own group; tests/test_api_contract.py pins the A290's endpoint map, so a release that changes it fails CI.

It also tracks the UI gate's render inputs in ui-tests/run.sh - the Home Assistant image and the four custom cards - which are pinned for a deterministic render, so without a bot they only move when someone remembers, and the gate drifts behind the Home Assistant users actually run.
And the Supervisor pilot's devcontainer and registry images in scripts/supervisor-pilot.sh, pinned by digest so a run is reproducible; without a bot the pilot would keep booting an old devcontainer.

And the CI tools: pytest, pytest-cov, bandit, pip-audit and playwright pinned inline in the workflows and the justfile, plus ruff and Trivy, whose versions the built-in Actions manager reads from their setup actions. Runtime Python packages are never pinned there: those steps install the hash-locked requirements.txt, so Python stays Dependabot's.

packageRules.description: One PR for all GitHub Actions, matching the grouping Dependabot used before this change.
Base and build-stage images move independently of the add-on, so keep them in their own PR to be container-verified on their own.
The shared core is a runtime-code change, never a routine bump. Keep it on its own PR so the build-and-boot gate applies to it alone.

The UI gate's render inputs move together, as ui-tests/run.sh requires: one PR carrying the Home Assistant image and all four cards, so the gate on that PR confirms the exact combination it will then pin. groupSingleUpdates keeps a lone bump (e.g. only a new Home Assistant) on that same group branch rather than a per-dependency PR; Renovate's default does not apply group settings to a single update. separateMajorMinor is off for the same reason: a major (a new year for Home Assistant, a card's major version) would otherwise split into a second PR and the gate would never see the combination. It runs at any time rather than the repo's Saturday schedule: the gate's stable leg must track current stable (global rule), so a new Home Assistant release should reach a PR within hours, not up to a week.
packageRules.commitMessageTopic: the UI gate's Home Assistant and card pins

packageRules.description: The Supervisor pilot's images move on their own, apart from the add-on's base image and the UI gate: one PR carrying the devcontainer and the registry, so the pilot on that PR proves the new devcontainer still boots the Supervisor before it is pinned.
The five CI Python tools and nothing else: a runtime package pinned in a workflow would put Python under two bots, so anything else this manager finds is ignored.

The CI tools move together, on the repo's Saturday schedule, so the CI run on that PR tests the set it pins. A release waits 3 days before it is proposed; strict, so no branch exists (and no CI runs it) before then.
ruff and Trivy are versions the built-in Actions manager reads from their setup actions; they join the CI tools PR rather than the actions group.
Trivy waits a week: a malicious Trivy release (v0.69.4) is why it is pinned at all.
The workflows' Python is the add-on runtime's (the HA base image ships 3.14); it moves with the base image, by hand, never as a routine bump.

description: CORE_REF pins the shared renault-mqtt core by immutable commit SHA. No manifest declares it, so Dependabot cannot see it at all and it has only ever been bumped by hand.

The version comment and the SHA are captured together and rewritten as a pair, so the comment cannot drift away from the pin beneath it. This is the same shape as a SHA-pinned GitHub Action carrying a version comment.

Tag datasource, not the branch head: a bump should mean a released core, not merely the newest commit on main. If a release ever ships untagged, Renovate goes quiet rather than proposing a bump - the safe direction to fail.

The Home Assistant image the UI gate renders on. Stable releases only: the regex versioning rejects beta (2026.10.0b1), dev and the floating stable/latest tags, which made the gate flake before it was pinned. Home Assistant's monthly release is the version's minor here.
Cards the UI gate downloads as GitHub release assets (mushroom, button-card).
Strict vX.Y.Z versioning rather than semver-coerced, as for the jsDelivr cards below: only a v-prefixed three-part release is a candidate, so button-card's -dev pre-releases are never proposed.
Cards the UI gate fetches from jsDelivr at a git tag (card-mod, Bubble Card). jsDelivr serves the tag, so track tags.

Strict vX.Y.Z versioning, not semver-coerced: card-mod also carries bare legacy tags 4 to 14, which semver-coerced reads as 14.0.0 and proposes over v4.2.1 (seen on the r5 twin's dashboard), plus v4.2.1-202604 and -beta/-rc tags on both repos.

The devcontainer and registry images the Supervisor pilot runs (ADR 0002), each a quoted name:tag@digest. The tag must be the exact upstream tag (6-apps, 3), or the lookup fails silently and no update is ever offered.
The same rule as polygonal-zones' pilot, which this one is adapted from.

CI tools pinned inline as name==version on pip install lines in the workflows and the justfile. Recursive: first a non-comment line with pip install, then each pin on it; one line only, so keep pins off continuation lines. requirements.txt is not in these files and stays Dependabot's.
